name: Jonathan
bio:
Jonathan was the son of Gershom and grandson of Manasseh, a young man of the tribe of Levi. He had been living in Bethlehem before traveling to the hill country of Ephraim, where Micah hired him as his personal priest to serve the idols Micah had made (Judges 17:7-13 — the text at first calls him only "the Levite" or "the young man," revealing his name only in 18:30).

When scouts sent by the tribe of Dan passed through Micah's house, they recognized Jonathan's voice and questioned him about his situation; later, six hundred armed Danites arrived, took the carved idol, the ephod, and the household gods from Micah's house, and told Jonathan, "Isn't it better that you be a priest for a whole tribe and clan in Israel than for just one man's household?" Jonathan was pleased, took the idols, and went along with the people of Dan (Judges 18:3-20). He and his descendants went on to serve as priests for the tribe of Dan until the time the land was carried off into captivity, and Micah's carved idol remained set up and worshiped by the Danites throughout the period the house of God stood at Shiloh (Judges 18:30-31). Jonathan's choice vividly captures the spiritual chaos and corruption of the priesthood depicted at the close of the book of Judges.
